samples.summary: Frontend's copy of parseBlockStyle/serializeBlockStyle was not hardened alongside the backend's, so documents already carrying the poisoned attributes still read as NaN in the editor
samples.evidence: The diff hardens `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts` so a partial block style is neither written as the literal string "undefined" nor read back as NaN. The frontend reads and writes the *same* Yorkie Tree attributes with its own untouched implementation: `serializeBlockStyle` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:206-215) unconditionally does `String(style.lineHeight)` etc., and `parseBlockStyle` (same file, lines 217-226) does `if ('lineHeight' in attrs) partial.lineHeight = Number(attrs.lineHeight)` with no `Number.isFinite` guard and `if ('alignment' in attrs) partial.alignment = attrs.alignment` with no `typeof === 'string'` guard. Since the PUT validation accepted `style: {}` *before* this change too (`assertValidBlock` only checked `typeof b.style === 'object'`), any document already written by the old backend serializer holds `alignment: "undefined"` / `lineHeight: "undefined"`. The backend now heals those on read; the browser editor still turns them into NaN geometry (`normalizeBlockStyle` at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272 is a bare spread and keeps NaN) and, on the next block-style edit, re-serializes them as the string "NaN" back into the CRDT (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1511). The fix belongs in the frontend reader/writer, mirroring docs-tree.ts.

samples.summary: The new removeCellNodeStyle helper silently changed the removal semantics of the pre-existing applyCellSpan path from removeStyleByPath to an index-range tree.removeStyle
samples.evidence: `applyCellSpan` previously cleared `colSpan`/`rowSpan` with `tree.removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, attrsToRemove)`; the diff replaces that with `removeCellNodeStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:277-285), which computes `tree.pathToIndex(cellPath)` and calls `tree.removeStyle(from, from + 1, attrs)`. `tree.removeStyle` appears nowhere else in the repo (only `removeStyleByPath` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1463 and :1920 and `pathToIndex` at :925), the frontend package has no `tsc` lane at all, and the index arithmetic assumption ('a child node starts exactly at idx + 1') is asserted only in a comment. If the index range does not select the cell element node, unmerging a cell (`applyCellSpan(..., { colSpan: 1 })`) stops clearing the attribute in the CRDT. The existing regression tests for that path (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2097-2116) assert via `store.getDocument()`, i.e. the local cache — which the diff's own new tests deliberately bypass with `new YorkieDocStore(doc)` — so a CRDT-level regression on the span path would pass CI unnoticed and only surface for collaborators / after reload.

samples.summary: A second <a:srgbClr val> sink bypasses the new shared toRgbHexColor normalizer
samples.evidence: The diff establishes that `<a:srgbClr val>` must be a normalized `ST_HexColorRGB` and routes `colorChildXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:42) through `toRgbHexColor`. `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:83-84` writes the deck's 12 theme slots with `toSrgbHex()` (`hex.replace(/^#/, '').toUpperCase()`, line 64-66) — no normalization. The values come from `parseColorScheme` on an uploaded PPTX (packages/slides/src/import/pptx/theme.ts:74-83) and from the frontend theme editor, so a non-hex value (e.g. a CSS `rgb()` string) would still land in theme1.xml as an invalid attribute. It is `escapeXmlAttr`-wrapped, so this is a schema-validity gap, not injection.

samples.summary: Slides PPTX exporter imports the new runtime value from the browser entry of @wafflebase/docs, not the node entry the diff added it to
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/node.ts:94-100` adds `toRgbHexColor` specifically because 'the slides PPTX exporter (a Node consumer via @wafflebase/slides/node) ... needs it, so it must be reachable from this entry'. But the consumers import it from the package root: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:1` and `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:3` both do `import { toRgbHexColor } from '@wafflebase/docs'`, which resolves to the DOM-bearing browser entry (`packages/slides/vite.config.ts:17` aliases it to `../docs/src/index.ts`). These files are reachable from `packages/slides/src/node.ts:171` (`exportPptx`). The pattern pre-exists (`import/pptx/text.ts:2` also value-imports from the root entry), so this may be intentional — but then the `node.ts` re-export the diff added has no importer, which is also what knip's unused-export rule looks at.

finding.summary: Frontend's copy of parseBlockStyle/serializeBlockStyle was not hardened alongside the backend's, so documents already carrying the poisoned attributes still read as NaN in the editor

Since the PUT validation accepted `style: {}` *before* this change too (`assertValidBlock` only checked `typeof b.style === 'object'`), any document already written by the old backend serializer holds `alignment: "undefined"` / `lineHeight: "undefined"`. The backend now heals those on read; the browser editor still turns them into NaN geometry (`normalizeBlockStyle` at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272 is a bare spread and keeps NaN) and, on the next block-style edit, re-serializes them as the string "NaN" back into the CRDT (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1511). verdict.reason: Verified independently. Backend docs-tree.ts:158-189 now guards serialization (typeof string / Number.isFinite) and parsing (skips non-finite) of block style attributes, with a comment noting normalizeBlockStyle cannot be relied on. The frontend's parallel implementation over the SAME Yorkie Tree attribute names is unhardened: yorkie-doc-store.ts:206-215 unconditionally writes `alignment: style.alignment` and `String(style.lineHeight)` (yielding the literal "undefined"/"NaN" for absent or NaN fields), and :217-227 reads back with bare `'field' in attrs` + `Number(...)`, producing NaN. packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274 confirms normalizeBlockStyle is a bare spread that preserves NaN. The NaN then round-trips back into the CRDT via applyBlockStyle at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1505-1521 (serializeBlockStyle(merged) at :1511), and partial styles from API-loaded documents can be poisoned at first write via buildBlockNode (:341, :350) and the block-split path (:2073). This is a shared wire contract changed on one side with the other-package consumer left on the old behaviour — in-lane for blast radius and blocking at major.

finding.summary: The new removeCellNodeStyle helper silently changed the removal semantics of the pre-existing applyCellSpan path from removeStyleByPath to an index-range tree.removeStyle
finding.evidence: `applyCellSpan` previously cleared `colSpan`/`rowSpan` with `tree.removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, attrsToRemove)`; the diff replaces that with `removeCellNodeStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:277-285), which computes `tree.pathToIndex(cellPath)` and calls `tree.removeStyle(from, from + 1, attrs)`. `tree.removeStyle` appears nowhere else in the repo (only `removeStyleByPath` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1463 and :1920 and `pathToIndex` at :925), the frontend package has no `tsc` lane at all, and the index arithmetic assumption ('a child node starts exactly at idx + 1') is asserted only in a comment. If the index range does not select the cell element node, unmerging a cell (`applyCellSpan(..., { colSpan: 1 })`) stops clearing the attribute in the CRDT. The existing regression tests for that path (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2097-2116) assert via `store.getDocument()`, i.e. the local cache — which the diff's own new tests deliberately bypass with `new YorkieDocStore(doc)` — so a CRDT-level regression on the span path would pass CI unnoticed and only surface for collaborators / after reload.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described (removeCellNodeStyle at yorkie-doc-store.ts:277-285, used by applyCellStyle:2472 and applyCellSpan:2522), and the span tests do read the cache (getDocument:583-586). But the asserted failure mode — "if the index range does not select the cell element node, unmerging silently stops clearing colSpan in the CRDT and CI would not notice" — is contradicted by an in-repo CRDT-level test of the identical helper and identical cellPath arithmetic: tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2033-2047 clears backgroundColor via removeCellNodeStyle and reads it back through `new YorkieDocStore(doc)` (fresh parse of the Tree, cache bypassed), asserting the cell node's attribute is gone while a sibling attribute survives; :2053-2066 pins that the range does not reach inside the cell. The removal target depends only on cellPath (identical at :2470 and :2491), not on the attribute name, so the span path's removal is exercised by the same proven arithmetic — wrong index math would fail CI, not regress silently. Secondarily this is out of the blast-radius lane: both the helper and both call sites are in the changed code, and every external consumer (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:697,747,837 via the unchanged store.applyCellSpan contract in store.ts:126 / memory.ts:287) is unaffected; "is the index arithmetic correct" belongs to the correctness lens.

mergedFrom.summary: Slides PUT arm never validates the docs blocks its text elements carry, so the same alignment guard does not apply there

finding.summary: New `style.alignment` validation is bypassed by header/footer blocks in the same PUT body
finding.evidence: `assertValidDocsBody` only iterates `body.blocks` (docs-content.controller.ts:249-251), but `writeDocsRoot` also persists `document.header.blocks` and the footer counterpart verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:289-293). A PUT payload carrying `{ blocks: [], header: { marginFromEdge: 0, blocks: [{ id:'b1', type:'paragraph', style:{ alignment: 'center"/><w:jc w:val="right' }, inlines: [] }] } }` reaches Yorkie without ever passing through `assertValidBlockStyle`, and those same blocks are fed to `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` when header1.xml/footer1.xml are generated. The exporter's new `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` clamp is what still saves the file, so the API-level guard the diff advertises is only half-applied. Fix belongs in `assertValidDocsBody`: validate `header`/`footer` blocks too.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts a "new style.alignment validation" in the docs content PUT validator that header/footer blocks bypass. No such validation exists in this repository. `assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:254-312) is shape-only: for `style` it checks solely `typeof b.style === 'object'` (:271-273), and the comment at :265-270 states outright that style *values* are deliberately unconstrained because every OOXML sink resolves `alignment` through its own closed lookup. A repo-wide grep for `alignment` under packages/backend/src turns up only tests, `docs-tree.ts` serialize/parse, and that comment — there is no `assertValidBlockStyle` and no alignment allow-list. Consequently `body.blocks` and `header`/`footer.blocks` are validated identically (shape-only for the former, nothing for the latter): there is no guard to be "half-applied" and no differential bypass. Additionally, the injection sink the finding names is already closed on exactly the header/footer path it cites: docx-exporter.ts:109-124 feeds `doc.header`/`doc.footer` into `buildHeaderFooterXml` (:360-383), which maps each block through `blockToXml` (:366), which builds paragraph props via `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` (:186); that function clamps alignment with the closed Map lookup `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS.get(style.alignment) ?? 'left'` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:118-147), so a value like `center"/><w:jc w:val="right` can never reach a `w:jc` attribute from header1.xml/footer1.xml any more than from document.xml. The finding concedes this clamp holds. Nothing in the diff's advertised interface is bypassed by another entry point, so there is no blast-radius defect here.
